name: Mwatebu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Papuan Tip Austronesian; only Lithgow survey wordlists (1976, 1992); no descriptive phonology found.

sources.citation: Lithgow, David R. 1976. Austronesian languages: Milne Bay and adjacent islands (Milne Bay Province). In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages, 441-523. Pacific Linguistics C-39. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only a cluster-wide section 84 'STRESS' (p.475) for all Papuan Tip Cluster languages: vowel lengthening near the end of the phonological word (penult in Dobu); stress phonemic in Kilivila, Muyuw, Budibud, Misima; 'in all of the languages of PTC it seems that stress is predictable within certain word-classes', shifting one syllable toward the end under suffixation. Mwatebu itself is only located (para 42, p.457) and classified (paras 56, 69); nothing Mwatebu-specific about stress.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: 5 references total (Lithgow 1976, Lithgow 1992, Moseley 2010 atlas, Ethnologue 2009, World Oral Literature Project); zero grammar/phonology/sketch entries.

sources.citation: Lithgow, David. 1992. Language change on Fergusson and Normanby islands, Milne Bay Province, Papua New Guinea. In T. Dutton (ed.), Culture change, language change: case studies from Melanesia, 27-47. Pacific Linguistics C-120. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic/lexical-change study (Mwatebu mentioned pp. ~40-41 as a very small language undergoing massive lexical change toward Dobu). No occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent'.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU.

sources.note: Mwatebu does not appear in Ross's Papuan Tip data at all (a full-text search for stress/accent full text: zero hits); no stress statement applicable.
Stub; no phonology; cites only Ethnologue and a UN village-coordinates dataset.

sources.citation: Lithgow, Daphne & David Lithgow. Dobu phonology / Dobu-English dictionary materials (SIL, 1970s; Glottolog ref 71815 Lithgow 1977) -- nearest well-described relative (Dobu-Duau network)

sources.note: Not Mwatebu, but Lithgow 1976 p.471 says Mwatebu is grammatically closest to the Dobu family; a Dobu stress description is the best available proxy if the catalog ever admits inferred entries (it should be flagged as proxy, dobu1241).
